_what: Act VII's record: the words that go on screen, the windows they occupy, the measured letterbox, and the build parameters that produce the delivered master. It exists so act VII's inputs are COMMITTED rather than living only in ~/Videos/wolves-directors-cut, where nimbatus-review/render/run-final-hq.sh cuts it (#152). Without it a dialogue round (#102) has nowhere to land, and the plates can be re-rendered in the project while the film keeps playing the older cut. scripts/build_europa.py reads this; editing a line here changes the film.
_provenance: Every line of copy is the OWNER'S OWN, from #102's terse-pass table, reproduced VERBATIM -- including 'AN4-CH4K-12' and the asterisk in 'f*cking' -- with the BSHERMAN recast applied. The removed sign-off ('... disavow my existence. Tell the medic and the engineer I'll meet them there. Out.') stays removed; it lives on in #102 and the project's _backups/. The picture graph, the audio join, the reveal/endcard cards and their windows are a RECORD of what shipped (nimbatus-review/render/run-final-hq.sh), not a new edit. The pill windows are the one new authoring: #102's proposed schedule with the cold open compressed to clear the clock shot (see c02's _note).
title: Europa

trim._note: The delivered act is 97.266 s (2918 frames at 30 fps): the 110.2 s master is cut at 97.266 with the picture STREAM-COPIED, dropping the comic-cover tail (97.200-110.200), which is act VIII's reveal now (#178). The audio is faded out over its last 2.5 s and trimmed to 97.2. Every window below is on the delivered cut's own clock, which matches the master's clock for 0-97.2.

letterbox._note: 2.39:1, MEASURED on the plate-free source (wolves-directors-cut-europa-intro-hq.mp4): cropdetect limit=24 gives crop=1920:804:0:138, and a per-region signalstats pass confirms the top and bottom 138 px bands are pure video-black (YAVG ~16.0). Measuring the DELIVERED master instead reads 1920:902:0:140 at dialogue moments -- that is the baked-in PRE-terse pills being detected as content, which is precisely what this rebuild removes. Dialogue plates seat INSIDE the bottom matte and never cover the picture.

reveal._note: The credit nameplate, on the Exo walk-up. It sits RIGHT to stay clear of the Guardian walking up centre, and holds the whole walk-up, clearing at 90.0 so the announcement gets 6.4 s of its own. Class reads 'Revenant Hunter' to match the Beyond Light footage; the website's authored Gunslinger (Solar) labels her Into the Light appearance instead, so the two legitimately differ -- do not 'correct' it. The credit is Laura Santamaria's, unchanged: the Orlin recast (#73) stays open and is NOT landed here.
reveal._not_repo_rendered: The nameplate card is NOT rendered from this record. It is the project's reveal-options/D-2.png (a 3840x2160 RGBA card), whose copy is Laura's authored Guardian identity, reproduced verbatim and never written here -- same division of labour as act IV's reveal. Giving the reveal a repo-rendered card is separate work.

endcard._note: The KubeCon announcement card ('Coming to KubeCon + Cloud Native Con NA / Salt Lake City, UT, USA / Kube of Destiny Located. Status: Calamitous'), project-supplied like the reveal. Runs to 97.2, 66 ms before the delivered cut ends. It is a full-frame card: a still input that was NOT opened with -framerate 30 was the original ghost-frame bug, so the record's encode.loop_framerate is load-bearing.
endcard._not_repo_rendered: Rendered by the project's render-endcards.mjs from endcard.html; consumed here as an existing PNG, same as the reveal.

picture._note: The concat reproduces nimbatus-review/render/run-final-hq.sh's [b0a][bsp][b0b][b1][b2][b3] graph verbatim: 57.5 + 5.1333 + 21.5 + 4.0667 + 9.0 = 97.2 s of content, then the 13 s comic cover to a 110.2 s master. THIS is the restyle the owner asked for: the delivered master's pills were screenshotted from the project's own plate.html by playwright (nimbatus-review/render/render-plates.mjs), a chrome that matches nothing else in the show; a rebuild from this record renders every pill with plate.py, the same renderer acts IV and V use. _timing: at + dur are tools/plate.py's own manifest fields, so this file renders with plate.py render --manifest unmodified. fade_out_at is absolute film time, matching the ffmpeg fade=t=out:st= it generates; the house fade pair (in 0.6, out 0.25 completing 0.05 s before the window boundary) keeps a plate from ever ghosting into the next shot.
